status.statement: Engineering evidence prepared by a tool; not a subject review. An engineering agent cannot sign this packet.

taskIntent.purpose: Predict, then observe, how the directions of two vectors u and v in a right-handed 3D frame determine the angle between them, their dot product and their cross product.

stages.instruction: Get oriented: turn the 3D view or use the orientation presets, find the positive x, y and z axes, and compare the view with the three flat projections.
Before any angle or product is shown, look at u and v in space and in the projections, and predict how they are related.

response.prompt: Is the angle between u and v acute, a right angle or obtuse? What sign do you expect for u·v, and which way do you expect u × v to point?

stages.instruction: Change the components of u and v and watch the angle θ, the dot product u·v and the relationship. Compare what you see with your prediction.
Once the cross product u × v is shown as well, change u and v, swap their order and compare its direction and length with the angle between them.
Explain in your own words how the directions of u and v determine the angle, the dot product and the cross product.

response.prompt: How do the directions of u and v determine the sign of u·v, the size of θ and the direction and length of u × v?

stages.instruction: Explore freely: change both vectors, use the scenarios, turn the 3D view and compare the projections and values.

taskFamilies.description: Host-owned prediction request about the angle between two vectors in space, the sign of their dot product and the direction of their cross product. The host owns the response, its capture and any evaluation.
Host-owned explanation request about how the directions of two vectors determine their angle, dot product and cross product. The host owns the response, its capture and any evaluation.

Host-owned later task with new vectors or another representation, such as a projection-only or table-only version. Its prompts, held-out items and scoring stay with the host and are not part of this catalogue.

derivation.citation: Derivation written for this catalogue: u·v = Σ u_i v_i = |u||v| cos θ; u×v = (u_y v_z − u_z v_y, u_z v_x − u_x v_z, u_x v_y − u_y v_x) with e_x × e_y = e_z in a right-handed frame, so |u×v| = |u||v| sin θ and |u×v|² + (u·v)² = |u|²|v|² (Lagrange's identity). Hence θ = atan2(|u×v|, u·v) ∈ [0, π], defined when u ≠ 0 and v ≠ 0; u×v = 0 exactly when a vector is zero or u and v are parallel or antiparallel, and then it has no direction. Not independently reviewed.

Study Harness visualizer implementation report §12.4 (spatial vector orientation: two vectors, their angle, dot and cross products with declared handedness, coordinate projections, orientation presets, exact numeric alternatives, parallel, antiparallel, orthogonal and zero-vector checks) and §11 (3D equivalents).

assumptions: u and v are dimensionless vectors in a right-handed Cartesian frame; their components are exact IEEE-754 double values.
The cross product follows the right-hand rule: e_x × e_y = e_z, e_y × e_z = e_x, e_z × e_x = e_y.
Two nonzero vectors are classified with the tolerance τ = 1/10¹²: parallel or antiparallel when sin θ ≤ τ, orthogonal when |cos θ| ≤ τ, decided exactly from the inputs.

Evaluation is deterministic within one JavaScript engine: θ, the unit directions and the angle arc use Math.atan2, Math.cos, Math.sin and exponentiation, which ECMAScript lets each engine approximate, so their last bits can differ between engines; the dot and cross products, the lengths and the relationship are computed exactly and are the same on every engine.
limitations: Dot products, cross-product components and lengths are rounded once from exact values; θ and the unit direction are computed from those rounded, rescaled values and agree with exact references to a few units in the last place.

The classification is a tolerance decision on exact values, not a property of displayed digits: decimal inputs that are not exactly proportional in binary can be parallel within the tolerance while u×v is a tiny nonzero vector with a defined, input-sensitive direction.

A nonzero result smaller than the smallest representable number is a numerical-limit status, never 0; an inexact result below the smallest normal double is reported as a reduced-precision approximation.

The cross product is drawn at true scale and can leave the default view; the unit direction is drawn with length 1. The angle arc is sampled at 33 points; the polyline between samples is a drawing aid.
Projections onto coordinate planes drop one component each, so a single projection cannot show whether two vectors are parallel or orthogonal in space.

conventions.coordinate: Right-handed Cartesian frame with axes x, y, z and e_x × e_y = e_z; u and v are free vectors drawn from the common origin. The xy projection is viewed from +z, the xz projection from −y and the yz projection from +x, each with its first named axis to the right and the second up.
conventions.angle: θ is the unsigned angle between u and v in radians, 0 ≤ θ ≤ π, computed as atan2(|u×v|, u·v). Degree display converts at the presentation boundary (1° = π/180 rad); the canonical value stays in radians.

ux.label: u x component
ux.description: The x component of the vector u, drawn from the origin. Every component from -3 to 3 is allowed, including 0.

uy.label: u y component
uy.description: The y component of the vector u, drawn from the origin. Every component from -3 to 3 is allowed, including 0.

uz.label: u z component
uz.description: The z component of the vector u, drawn from the origin. Every component from -3 to 3 is allowed, including 0.

vx.label: v x component
vx.description: The x component of the vector v, drawn from the origin. Every component from -3 to 3 is allowed, including 0.

vy.label: v y component
vy.description: The y component of the vector v, drawn from the origin. Every component from -3 to 3 is allowed, including 0.

vz.label: v z component
vz.description: The z component of the vector v, drawn from the origin. Every component from -3 to 3 is allowed, including 0.

u.label: Vector u
u.meaning: The vector u = (u_x, u_y, u_z), equal to its three parameters.
u.coordinateFrame: right-handed Cartesian frame (x, y, z), origin shared by u and v
u.signConvention: Components (x, y, z) along the positive axes of the right-handed frame, where e_x × e_y = e_z.

v.label: Vector v
v.meaning: The vector v = (v_x, v_y, v_z), equal to its three parameters.
v.coordinateFrame: right-handed Cartesian frame (x, y, z), origin shared by u and v
v.signConvention: Components (x, y, z) along the positive axes of the right-handed frame, where e_x × e_y = e_z.

u.norm.label: Length of u
u.norm.meaning: |u| = √(u_x² + u_y² + u_z²), rounded once from its exact value.
u.norm.coordinateFrame: right-handed Cartesian frame (x, y, z), origin shared by u and v
u.norm.signConvention: A length: never negative; 0 only for the zero vector.

v.norm.label: Length of v
v.norm.meaning: |v| = √(v_x² + v_y² + v_z²), rounded once from its exact value.
v.norm.coordinateFrame: right-handed Cartesian frame (x, y, z), origin shared by u and v
v.norm.signConvention: A length: never negative; 0 only for the zero vector.

dot.label: Dot product
dot.meaning: u·v = u_x v_x + u_y v_y + u_z v_z = |u|·|v|·cos θ, rounded once from its exact value. It does not depend on the order of u and v.
dot.coordinateFrame: right-handed Cartesian frame (x, y, z), origin shared by u and v
dot.signConvention: Positive for an acute angle, 0 for a right angle or a zero vector, negative for an obtuse angle.

angle.label: Angle between u and v
angle.meaning: θ = atan2(|u×v|, u·v), the unsigned angle between u and v in radians, 0 ≤ θ ≤ π. Undefined (ZERO_VECTOR) when u or v is the zero vector, because a zero vector has no direction.
angle.coordinateFrame: right-handed Cartesian frame (x, y, z), origin shared by u and v
angle.signConvention: Unsigned: the same for (u, v) and (v, u); 0 when u and v point the same way, π when they point in opposite directions.

relationship.label: Relationship of u and v
relationship.meaning: Classification with the declared tolerance τ = 1e-12 (the rational 1/10¹², applied exactly to the inputs): parallel when sin θ ≤ τ and u·v > 0, antiparallel when sin θ ≤ τ and u·v < 0, orthogonal when |cos θ| ≤ τ, oblique otherwise, undefined-zero-vector when u or v is the zero vector. Never derived from displayed digits.

cross.label: Cross product
cross.meaning: u×v = (u_y v_z − u_z v_y, u_z v_x − u_x v_z, u_x v_y − u_y v_x), each component rounded once from its exact value. Its length is |u|·|v|·sin θ and it is perpendicular to both u and v; it is the zero vector exactly when u or v is zero or u and v are parallel or antiparallel.
cross.coordinateFrame: right-handed Cartesian frame (x, y, z), origin shared by u and v
cross.signConvention: Right-hand rule: with the fingers of the right hand turning from u toward v through θ, the thumb points along u×v; e_x × e_y = e_z, and v×u = −(u×v).

cross.norm.label: Length of the cross product
cross.norm.meaning: |u×v| = |u|·|v|·sin θ, the area of the parallelogram spanned by u and v, rounded once from its exact value.
cross.norm.coordinateFrame: right-handed Cartesian frame (x, y, z), origin shared by u and v
cross.norm.signConvention: A length: never negative; 0 only for the zero vector.

cross.direction.label: Direction of the cross product
cross.direction.meaning: Unit vector u×v / |u×v|, normal to the plane of u and v. Undefined (NO_CROSS_DIRECTION) whenever u×v = 0 exactly (a zero vector, or parallel or antiparallel vectors); no direction is ever chosen arbitrarily. Defined for every nonzero u×v, including nearly parallel vectors classified as parallel within the tolerance, where it is sensitive to tiny input changes.
cross.direction.coordinateFrame: right-handed Cartesian frame (x, y, z), origin shared by u and v

u.xy.label: u projected onto the xy plane
u.xy.meaning: Orthogonal projection of u onto the xy plane: its components (x, y), with the third component dropped.
u.xy.coordinateFrame: xy plane of the right-handed frame, viewed from +z (z toward the viewer)
u.xy.signConvention: Components (x, y) along the positive axes of that plane.

v.xy.label: v projected onto the xy plane
v.xy.meaning: Orthogonal projection of v onto the xy plane: its components (x, y), with the third component dropped.
v.xy.coordinateFrame: xy plane of the right-handed frame, viewed from +z (z toward the viewer)
v.xy.signConvention: Components (x, y) along the positive axes of that plane.

u.xz.label: u projected onto the xz plane
u.xz.meaning: Orthogonal projection of u onto the xz plane: its components (x, z), with the third component dropped.
u.xz.coordinateFrame: xz plane of the right-handed frame, viewed from −y (y away from the viewer)
u.xz.signConvention: Components (x, z) along the positive axes of that plane.

v.xz.label: v projected onto the xz plane
v.xz.meaning: Orthogonal projection of v onto the xz plane: its components (x, z), with the third component dropped.
v.xz.coordinateFrame: xz plane of the right-handed frame, viewed from −y (y away from the viewer)
v.xz.signConvention: Components (x, z) along the positive axes of that plane.

u.yz.label: u projected onto the yz plane
u.yz.meaning: Orthogonal projection of u onto the yz plane: its components (y, z), with the third component dropped.
u.yz.coordinateFrame: yz plane of the right-handed frame, viewed from +x (x toward the viewer)
u.yz.signConvention: Components (y, z) along the positive axes of that plane.

v.yz.label: v projected onto the yz plane
v.yz.meaning: Orthogonal projection of v onto the yz plane: its components (y, z), with the third component dropped.
v.yz.coordinateFrame: yz plane of the right-handed frame, viewed from +x (x toward the viewer)
v.yz.signConvention: Components (y, z) along the positive axes of that plane.

suite.author: Reference cases for report §12.4 (handedness, parallel, antiparallel, orthogonal, oblique and zero vectors) plus tolerance-boundary and numerical-limit cases. Integer cases are derived by hand; every stored value is the output of the exact oracle tests/reference/oracles/vector-orientation-3d.ts, which shares no code with the catalogue kernel.
suite.review: No independent human subject reviewer has approved these cases. Automated agreement is engineering evidence only.

derivedFrom.conversion: Converted by explorable-models activity tooling: case IDs, labels, provenance, parameters and tolerances copied unchanged; quantity expectations restated as explorable-models.reference-fixtures 1.0 expectations.

notCovered: The angle-arc flag and the exact geometry of u, v and their projections are checked by tests/reference/activities/vector-orientation-3d.test.ts.

stages.instruction: Get oriented: turn the 3D view or use the orientation presets, find the positive x, y and z axes, and compare the view with the three flat projections.
Before any angle or product is shown, look at u and v in space and in the projections, and predict how they are related.

response.prompt: Is the angle between u and v acute, a right angle or obtuse? What sign do you expect for u·v, and which way do you expect u × v to point?

stages.instruction: Change the components of u and v and watch the angle θ, the dot product u·v and the relationship. Compare what you see with your prediction.
Once the cross product u × v is shown as well, change u and v, swap their order and compare its direction and length with the angle between them.
Explain in your own words how the directions of u and v determine the angle, the dot product and the cross product.

response.prompt: How do the directions of u and v determine the sign of u·v, the size of θ and the direction and length of u × v?

stages.instruction: Explore freely: change both vectors, use the scenarios, turn the 3D view and compare the projections and values.
